kurz: Fondue is a cheese [[emulsion|emulsion]]. Wine and starch hold it together; too much heat makes it fall apart into fat and strings.
bild_im_kopf: Like a sauce that only holds together in its comfort zone.

schluesselmomente.schritt: Grate the cheese finely and mix it with a little cornflour
schluesselmomente.warum: Starch coats the protein and prevents lumps.

schluesselmomente.schritt: Heat white wine and stir in the cheese in batches
schluesselmomente.warum: The [[saeure|acid]] in the wine keeps the [[kaese|cheese]] protein supple.

schluesselmomente.schritt: Only simmer gently, stirring constantly (in a figure of eight)
schluesselmomente.warum: Too much heat makes the protein contract and the fat seep out.

schluesselmomente.schritt: If it splits: a splash of lemon and a little starch slurry
schluesselmomente.warum: Acid and starch bring the emulsion back.
